history.dynasty: Yadava (legendary origins) / Chanda Rao More (present structure)
history.summary: Ancient Shiva temple in the village of Kshetra Mahabaleshwar (Old Mahabaleshwar), about 5–7 km north of Mahabaleshwar town — distinct from the newer Panchganga temple complex although both stand in the old kshetra. The self-originated (swayambhu) Mahalingam, rudraksha-shaped, is venerated as Trigunatmaka and locally held superior to the twelve jyotirlingas. Some sources give 13th-century Yadava origins; others credit the present structure to the Chanda Rao More dynasty in the 16th century — BUILT-DATE CONFLICT, flag. Legend records Shivaji weighing his mother Jijabai in gold here and giving it in charity. Nearby stand the Atibaleshwar temple, the Krishnabai temple, and the Panchganga shrine where the Krishna, Koyna, Venna, Gayatri and Savitri are said to meet. name: Kshetra Mahabaleshwar Temple
town_description: Kshetra Mahabaleshwar (Old Mahabaleshwar) is a historical hill village in the Western Ghats, Satara district, Maharashtra, about 7 km from Mahabaleshwar town at ~1,300 m elevation. It is the ancient sacred core of the region, home to the Mahabaleshwar, Atibaleshwar, Panchganga and Krishnabai temples, and is considered one of the holiest Shaivite sites of the Deccan.

travel.railway: Satara or Wathar railway station (~60 km)
travel.road: Old Mahabaleshwar is ~7 km from Mahabaleshwar town via Satara Road; Mahabaleshwar town is ~230 km by road from Mumbai

visitor_information.best_time: December to February; Mahashivratri and Shravan are the main festival periods
